_comment: Tracked deprecations awaiting removal. The deprecation-reaper workflow reads this file weekly, looks up when each entry's PR merged (its exact mergedAt timestamp), and once mergedAt + grace has elapsed it opens/refreshes a tracking issue and pings the owners. Entries whose PR is not merged yet are ignored, so the clock only starts at merge. Remove an entry once its functions are deleted.

deprecations.description: Remove the public pack_four_int8_into_uint32, create_random_vector_of_int8, pack_four_uint8_into_uint32, and create_random_vector_of_uint8 functions and their int8.hpp/uint8.hpp headers after the grace period. There is no public replacement. All test callers use independent tt::test_utils copies under tests/tt_metal/test_utils/; keep those copies. Delete the legacy implementations and remove their entries from tt_metal/impl/sources.cmake and the public headers from tt_metal/sources.cmake.

Legacy copy / eltwise-unary init API: copy_tile_init, copy_tile_to_dst_init_short, copy_tile_to_dst_init_short_with_dt in tt_metal/hw/inc/api/compute/tile_move_copy.h and unary_op_init_common, init_sfpu in tt_metal/hw/inc/api/compute/eltwise_unary/eltwise_unary.h. Replaced by compute_kernel_hw_startup(icb, ocb) + copy_init(icb); data-format reconfiguration via reconfig_data_format_srca. Deprecation messages state a fixed removal date of September 20th, 2026.

The Runtime API entry points that identify a command queue by raw id are deprecated in favor of overloads taking MeshCommandQueue& (tt-metal#51559): BeginTraceCapture(MeshDevice*, uint8_t) -> MeshDevice::begin_mesh_trace(MeshCommandQueue&), Synchronize(MeshDevice*, std::optional<uint8_t>, ...) -> Synchronize(MeshDevice&, ttsl::optional_reference<MeshCommandQueue>, ...), MeshDevice::{begin,end,replay}_mesh_trace(uint8_t, ...) -> the same members taking MeshCommandQueue&, and MeshEvent(uint32_t, MeshDevice*, uint32_t, const MeshCoordinateRange&) -> MeshEvent(uint32_t, MeshCommandQueue&, const MeshCoordinateRange&). All in-repo call sites are already migrated; the id-based overloads remain only for external callers during the grace period. The cleanup PR deletes them and their definitions in distributed.cpp, mesh_device.cpp and mesh_event.cpp, leaving only the MeshCommandQueue& forms.
